Order:

entities.text: High Court Of Andhra Pradesh :: Amaravati
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioners.

Also heard learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition representing respondents 2 to 5, who placed a copy of the written instructions dated 04.10.2023 for perusal of this Court and Mr. M. Solomon Raju, learned Standing Counsel for NHAI.

2. The Writ Petition is filed seeking to declare the action of the respondents 2 to 4 in not taking action on the letter addressed by the 2nd respondent dated 12.10.2022 for payment of enhancement of compensation on par with other awardees as per the award passed by the 3rd respondent dated 17.03.2022 in Rc.No.G1/NH/2616-1/2017 as illegal, arbitrary, against the principles of natural justice and for consequential direction to the 2nd and 4th respondents to take steps for payment of enhanced compensation.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that petitioners purchased an extent of Ac.0.60 cents in Sy.No.132-1 of Lepakshi Village for a valuable consideration in the year 2019 and that they are in possession and enjoyment of the same.

He submits that pursuant to a Notification issued by the 3rd respondent for acquisition of land in Sy.No.452-2A and 2B of an extent of Ac.24.95cents of Lekpakshi Village and Mandal under the provisions of National Highways Act and determination of compensation payable in terms of the said Act., an enquiry was conducted by the 3rd respondent and an award was passed on 17.03.2022.

He submits that the petitioners have not accepted the compensation awarded by the competent authority i.e., 3rd respondent and made a representation S Anji Naik vs The Union Of India on 11 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159152183/
1 dated 27.09.2022 to the 2nd respondent i.e., Arbitrator/District Collector requesting for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: He submits that the 2nd respondent vide communication dated 12.10.2022 requested the 4th respondent to take necessary action as per the Rules and submit remarks / report along with supporting documents.

He submits that despite reply of the 4th respondent dated 06.01.2023 recommending enhancement of compensation, so far no action has been taken by the 2nd respondent and therefore, the petitioners are constrained to file this present Writ Petition.
4. The learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition made his submissions with reference to the instructions dated 04.10.2023 referred to above.
5. This Court has considered the submissions made and perused the material on record.
6. Section 3G of National Highways Act., deals with determination of the amount payable as compensation.

Section 3G(5) provides that if the amount determined by the competent authority under Sub-Section (1) or Sub-Section (2) is not acceptable to either of the parties, the amount shall,
on an application by either of the parties, be determined by the arbitrator to be appointed by the Central Government.

Section 3G(6) of the Act., contemplates that subject to the provisions of the Act, the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (26 of 1996) shall apply to every arbitration under the National Highways Act.
7. It is not in dispute that the District Collector of the concerned District is notified as Arbitrator.
Under the National Highways Act.

Being a statutory Arbitrator, the District Collector has to discharge functions to adjudicate as to whether the compensation as awarded by the competent authority is just and adequate or the same needs to be enhanced or reduced on an application by either of the parties.

It is an independent statutory function and the provisions of the Arbitrator &
Conciliation Act, 1996 are also applicable.
8. Be that as it may.

As seen from the written instructions dated 04.10.2023, it would appear that the petitioners' representation dated 27.09.2022 is well within examination and compensation/
award is yet to be passed on the same.

The relevant portion of the instructions reads as follows:-
"At this juncture, where their representation dated:
27-09-2022 relating to payment of higher compensation is pending which is a financial matter and relating to state exchequer, hurried decision cannot be taken.

Further, it is prayed that, numerous aspects including repercussions have, to be examined and appropriate decision can only be passed after giving sufficient opportunity of hearing to the Writ Petitioners."
9.

As noted above, the 2nd respondent is required to discharge his functions as Arbitrator and therefore, this Court see no justification on the part of the 2nd respondent in keeping the representation of the petitioners dated 27.09.2022 for enhancement of compensation pending for the last one year.

Being an arbitrator and independent body, he has to examine the entitlement or S Anji Naik vs The Union Of India on 11 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159152183/
2 otherwise of the claim for enhancement of the compensation, without taking into consideration the other aspects, much less about the state exchequer, repercussions, etc.
10.

entities.text: S Anji Naik vs The Union Of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the matter in its entirety, this Court is inclined to dispose of the Writ Petition with a direction to the 2nd respondent i.e., Arbitrator to discharge his functions, as such, in terms of the National Highways Act., and pass appropriate order on the petitioners' representation / application dated 27.09.2022 for enhancement of the compensation, strictly in accordance with Law, as expeditiously as possible, within a period of six weeks, from the date of receipt of copy of this Order.
It is needless to mention that before passing orders, the petitioners shall be afforded an opportunity of hearing.
Accordingly, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, all pending applications shall stand closed.
